444:

the real Docent, escaped today.
445:
Hard to believe, but true.
It's dangerous for you to look like him.
446:
Could it wait till tomorrow? It's New Year,
and they've been trying, in their own way.
447:
We're out in the country.
I doubt Docent could find us.
448:
All right, but don't leave the house!
Oh, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife. Here's her reply,
addressed to him.
450:
- Promise you'll have lunch with us on the first?
- We promise!
451:
Such a nice woman. Shame her father's
a fence and a profiteer.
452:
What's all this shouting? Who said you could go out?
- Here he comes... The not-so-good person.
454:
The New Year has arrived. I wish for all of you
to make a fresh start this year.
455:
Anything may happen, but know this:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you,
and I'll find you. I promise.
457:
- And now... One moment...
- Where's he off to?
458:
Who knows? You can't make sense
of him anymore.
459:
What's to make sense of? He says he'll find us
wherever we are and slit our throats.
461:
They say he went like this across Pockmark's
throat with a razor. - The jackal's gone feral.
462:
Who's come to see you? Father Frost!
And he's brought presents for you!
463:
- Come here, Fedya. - What have I done?
- Come on. Wear these in good health. Slippers.
464:
- What do I need them for? I don't have a home.
- You will. You've got your whole life ahead of you.
465:
- For now, they'll come in handy in prison. Wear them.
- Always predicting the worst.
466:
This is for you, Vasya... And this is yours,
Gavrila Petrovich. - Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- And this is yours too.
469: Sour stuff. It's dull without vodka.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471: We could just sit and have a heart-to-heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor. I'm not having
a heart-to-heart with you. - We could play a game.
473:
Listen to him! Think I'll play cards with you?
You've got nine aces in your deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
then you use its last letter, W: Warsaw.
Then you use W again: Wellington. See?
477: Now you, Fedya. A city beginning with N.
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- All right. Then you need a city beginning with A.
- Dzhambul. - What has Dzhambul got to do with it?
480:
It's warm there. It's my home.
My mother lives there.
481:
Let's try this, then. I'll go out,
you hide something, and I'll find it.
482:
- You'd be better off finding the helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We'll hide it, and he'll peek through a hole?
- Then you go out and hide it.
484:
Make sure I don't peek.
Why me? Anything happens, it's always Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your trap, you little wretch!
- Your trap, your trap...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- Did you have a mom and dad?
- I did.
488: Why are you so mean? Why are you like a dog?
490:
- You came on your own.
- Oh, you're here too.
491:
I tried coming to your place,
but I sensed a trap.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Keep walking.
495:
- Sorry to have troubled you for nothing, doctor.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea,
and let him sleep. - Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499: "Dear Dad, we found out you're in prison
500:
and were very happy, because we thought
you were dead."
501:
What swine told Gloom's little kid
his dad was in prison?
502:
"Mom was happy too. When your letter came,
she cried all day.
503:
Before that, she told me
you were a test pilot."
505:
"I'm glad you're alive anyway,
because Mom says
506: you're a good man, just weak-willed."
507:
That's right! Weak-willed enough to steal
our money and blame the taxi driver.
508:
Get out! I'll knock your block off,
you rotten radish!
510:
Aren't you ashamed? You're forty years old,
half your lives already gone.
511:
What's behind you? What do you have now?
What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, nothing decent at all!
Come to your senses before it's too late. That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we've got to get out.
That doctor will report us to the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I took a razor to her throat...
515: She's in the well. Go look for yourself.
516: How much time did I have? One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten
and the apartment? Say ten!
520:
And I'm supposed to put up with that snake
for a lousy fourteen years?
521:
The one who put the old woman in the well?
Do what you like. I'm going to the police.
522: Go on! He won't hurt you.
523:
What about you? Will you put up with him
till the day you die?
524:
Vasya, I told him earlier
that I had a cold, and he...
525:
Enough about your cold! I'm sick of it.
Come here...
527:
- What are you doing?
- Cleaning the carpet.
528:
Well, comrades. The comedy's over.
First, I'm taking this off.
530:
I'll serve my time, and that's it.
I'm going straight! I'll get a job.
531:
- Doing what? Guarding my hometown collective farm.
- Why a guard?
532:
I could clear snow, lay bricks,
or be an interpreter. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought back helmet!
Who's Docent? A crook.
534:
- Plenty of crooks, but only one helmet.
- They'd reduce our sentences for the helmet.
535:
Where did he put it?
We searched everywhere.
536:
Crook! I told you I had a cold,
and all you said was, "I'll rip your trap."
537:
- You made me dive in that freezing weather!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us. Remember?
He said he'd fish, and I should dive.
539:
- Wait. What did he say about the fish?
- "I'm fishing through a hole in the ice.
540:
Can you swim, Kosoy?"
- That's where he hid the helmet! In that hole!
541:
Of course! I remember now, the rotten radish!
The hole in the ice, in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you speak up, you jerk?
You could've left a note before hanging yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- What about him?
- Let them fetch him. I'm not carrying that great lump. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing there.
- It's on the bottom. Someone has to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens, it's always Kosoy.
Vasya, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can't! It's cold. I'll get sick.
548:
- You were hanging yourself just now, and now you're afraid of a cold!
- Greetings, sports fans!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd kill you, but I haven't got time!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And another one back at the country house.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich! Well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we hand in, the better.
